news.titleTr: Akbank'tan 2,5 trilyon TL'lik dev hedef: Kaan Gür COP31'de açıkladı
news.summaryTr: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, COP31 kapsamında CNBC-e'ye yaptığı açıklamada, bankanın 2030 yılına kadar 2,5 trilyon TL sürdürülebilir finansman sağlamayı hedeflediğini söyledi. Gür, bu tutarın yarısını sanayide yeşil dönüşüme ayırmayı planladıklarını belirtti.
news.articleText: Akbank'tan 2,5 trilyon TL'lik dev hedef: Kaan Gür COP31'de açıkladı - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, COP31 kapsamında CNBC-e'ye yaptığı açıklamada, bankanın 2030 yılına kadar 2,5 trilyon TL sürdürülebilir finansman sağlamayı hedeflediğini söyledi. Gür, bu tutarın yarısını sanayide yeşil dönüşüme ayırmayı planladıklarını belirtti. Antalya'da düzenlenen Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı'nda (COP31) CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtlayan Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman hedeflerini, sanayide yeşil dönüşüme yönelik çalışmalarını ve yeni iş birliklerini anlattı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Gür, Akbank'ın 9 Kasım'dan bu yana COP31'de 38 kişilik bir ekiple yer aldığını, zirve boyunca yaklaşık 35 etkinlik ve çeşitli imza törenleri gerçekleştireceklerini söyledi. COP31'de taahhütlerden uygulamaya geçiş konusunda güçlü bir kararlılık gördüklerini belirten Gür, Türkiye'nin coğrafi konumu, sanayi altyapısı ve entegrasyon kapasitesiyle dönüşümde liderlik fırsatına sahip olduğunu ifade etti. Gür, Türkiye'nin sanayide düşük karbonlu üretime geçişini hızlandırması halinde mevcut ihracat pazarlarındaki rekabet gücünü koruyabileceğini ve küresel tedarik zincirinde kendisini yeniden konumlandırabileceğini söyledi. Sürdürülebilir finansman desteği 905 milyar TL'yi aştı Akbank'ın sürdürülebilir finansman hedeflerine ilişkin bilgi veren Gür, 2021 yılında 200 milyar TL'lik finansman hedefiyle yola çıktıklarını, 2024 yılında ise bu hedefi 800 milyar TL'ye yükselttiklerini hatırlattı. Gür, bankanın bugüne kadar sağladığı toplam sürdürülebilir finansman desteğinin 905 milyar TL'yi aştığını belirterek, 2030 yılına kadar 2,5 trilyon TL'lik yeni bir hedef belirlediklerini açıkladı. Finansman büyüklüğünün yanı sıra ekonomiye sağlanan katkının da önemli olduğunu vurgulayan Gür, sağlanan finansmanın karbon emisyonlarını ne ölçüde azalttığı, rekabet gücüne ve istihdama ne kadar katkı sunduğu gibi göstergeleri takip ettiklerini ifade etti. Finansmanın yarısı sanayide yeşil dönüşüme Gür, 2,5 trilyon TL'lik sürdürülebilir finansman hedefinin yüzde 50'sini sanayide yeşil dönüşüme ayırmayı planladıklarını söyledi. Bu kapsamda sanayide yeşil dönüşüm için 1,25 trilyon TL'lik finansman öngörülüyor. Akbank'ın sürdürülebilir finansmanda öncelik verdiği alanları sanayide yeşil dönüşüm, sürdürülebilir tedarik zinciri, elektrifikasyon, sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme ve mavi finansman olarak sıralayan Gür, tarım bankacılığı, kadınların ekonomideki gücünün artırılması, gençlerin geleceğe hazırlanması ile sosyal ve dijital kapsayıcılığın da bankanın odak alanları arasında yer aldığını belirtti. Gür, sanayide yeşil dönüşümde finansman desteğinin yanı sıra teknoloji ve teknik yeterliliklerin de önem taşıdığını ifade ederek projelerin yapılabilir, kârlı ve geri ödenebilir bir yapıda kurgulanması gerektiğini söyledi. Uluslararası kuruluşlarla ortak finansman Türkiye'nin 2035 yılına kadar güneş ve rüzgâr enerjisinde 120 gigavatlık hedefi bulunduğunu hatırlatan Gür, enerji kapasitesinin artırılmasının yanı sıra şebeke altyapısı, enerji depolama ve elektrifikasyon alanlarında da yatırımlara ihtiyaç duyulduğunu belirtti. Akbank'ın Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (EBRD) ve Uluslararası Finans Kurumu (IFC) gibi uluslararası kuruluşlarla ortak fonlama imkânları geliştirdiğini aktaran Gür, teknoloji ve teknik beceriler konusunda da danışmanlık yaklaşımıyla hareket edeceklerini söyledi. Büyük işletmelerin üretim tesislerindeki dönüşümün yanı sıra tedarik zincirlerinde yer alan KOBİ'lerin de desteklenmesi gerektiğini belirten Gür, daha dirençli bir tarım ekosistemi, su verimliliği ve geri kazanım projelerinin de bankanın öncelikleri arasında bulunduğunu ifade etti. Gür, uluslararası finans kuruluşlarıyla yürütülen çalışmalar kapsamında yatırımcılara, sanayicilere ve KOBİ'lere farklı vade ve risk paylaşımı imkânları sunmayı hedeflediklerini kaydetti. Daikin ile yeni finansman program Gür, COP31 kapsamında Birleşmiş Milletler Kalkınma Programı'nın (UNDP) Cool Up programı çerçevesinde Daikin ile yeni bir sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme finansman programına imza attıklarını açıkladı. Programdan ağırlıklı olarak KOBİ'lerin yararlanacağını belirten Gür, soğuk zincir, depolama, lojistik ve sağlık sektörlerinde enerji verimliliğinin artırılması ve karbon emisyonlarının azaltılmasına yönelik yatırımların destekleneceğini söyledi. Türkiye'deki enerji tüketiminin yaklaşık yüzde 48'inin binalardan kaynaklandığını belirten Gür, binalardaki enerji tüketiminin üçte birini ise iklimlendirme sistemlerinin oluşturduğunu ifade etti. Gür, program kapsamında Daikin'in teknoloji, Akbank'ın finansman, Frankfurt School of Finance and Management'ın ise teknik destek sağladığını belirtti. Yeni iş birlikleri devam edecek Sürdürülebilir tedarik zinciri finansmanına da değinen Gür, Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası ile 2025 yılında başlattıkları risk paylaşımlı finansman programının gelişerek devam ettiğini söyledi. Gür, önümüzdeki dönemde yeni iş birliklerinin süreceğini belirterek Akbank'ın sanayicilere, KOBİ'lere ve müşterilerine yeşil dönüşüm sürecinde destek vermeye devam edeceğini ifade etti.

news.summary: The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments.

news.titleTr: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services
news.summaryTr: The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments.
news.articleText: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments. UK-based digital bank Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B round led by Octagon Partners, valuing the company at over $100 million. The funding will support Griffin’s plans to expand into card issuance and stablecoin services, according to a Thursday press release. Griffin plans to let companies offer branded retail and corporate debit cards through its platform, with credit cards to follow. The bank also plans to expand its stablecoin reserve services and add onchain cross-border payments. Griffin’s said its banking platform serves more than 300,000 retail and business customers through more than 80 companies. They include Uber, which uses Griffin to provide bank accounts to UK drivers. Griffin received its UK banking license in March 2024. The bank said recurring revenue at its September fiscal year-end was 3.2 times the prior year’s level, based on unaudited accounts. Paraag Davé, managing partner at Octagon, said he expects Griffin’s annual recurring revenue to exceed 10 million British pounds soon. Related: Deutsche Bank launches crypto custody for companies and institutions

news.summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.

news.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
news.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment. Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. Of the four million people claiming Pip in England and Wales, around 430,000 are aged between 16 and 24. In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. "I don't think you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them get into work," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme. 'Cannot assume' Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. 'Rebuilding system from scratch' In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. Disability groups have welcomed extra employment support, but expressed concern that disabled young people could lose out. James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" for young disabled people and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear". Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details families were "deeply anxious" about what they could mean for them. A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence. Responding on Thursday, Tory shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said Milburn was "right to say it's time to stop handing out cash for mild conditions". But she raised concern that spending more on work placements would simply "compensate for the jobs Labour have killed with their taxes and red tape". If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said. His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support. "It is a contract. People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added. A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month. news.articleText: Millions of Ebola dollars going missing as virus spreads, medical charity warns - Published Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) says while the outbreak remains "out of control", there is a "considerable disconnect" between what is disbursed and what gets to "patients, frontline workers and communities". "Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many frontline responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets," the charity says in a report. More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May. This makes it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded. MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised. This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest," it said. MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for. At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure. - What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? - Published15 September In its report, external, MSF cited "cases of healthcare workers not being paid or trained, ambulances left to run without fuel, a lack of supplies or support for frontline employees". It also mentioned Ebola monitoring "surveillance teams that exist on paper but are nowhere to be seen on the ground". "Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim. One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation. "Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres. According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency. MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent. It said the response was "too slow" in North Kivu province while Haut-Uélé remained "dramatically overlooked". In both provinces, MSF observed that teams were "inadequately resourced to respond effectively" with health facilities lacking essential items such as water, chlorine or triage systems. "This has turned some facilities into new centres of transmission, rather than places of care that contribute to containing the disease," MSF said. The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control. There are very few good roads in the area, making it very hard to travel around. The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria. On Wednesday, the last person infected with Ebola in Kenya was discharged, marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation. The Bundibugyo species is relatively rare and has no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way. news.articleText: 2,2 milyon kişinin GSS prim borcu siliniyor: 5,6 milyar liralık düzenleme YAYIN TARİHİ, 12 Kasım 2026 16:02 PAYLAŞ - AK Parti Grup Başkanı Abdullah Güler, 1 Ocak 2017 öncesine ait ödenmemiş GSS prim borçları ile bunlara bağlı gecikme cezası ve zamlarının silinmesini öngören düzenlemeyi açıkladı. - Düzenlemenin yasalaşması halinde 2 milyon 199 bin 860 kişinin toplam 5,6 milyar liralık borcu ortadan kalkacak. AK Parti Grup Başkanı Abdullah Güler, 1 Ocak 2017 öncesine ait ödenmemiş GSS prim borçları ile gecikme cezası ve zamlarına ilişkin dikkat çeken açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Güler, GSS prim borçları ile gecikme cezası ve zamlarının tamamen silinmesinin öngörüldüğünü açıkladı Düzenlemenin yasalaşması halinde 2 milyon 199 bin 860 kişinin toplam 5 milyar 627 milyon 666 bin liralık borcu ortadan kalkacak. Düzenlemeye ilişkin açıklamasında Güler, şu ifadeleri kullandı: “1 Ocak 2017 öncesine ait ödenmemiş Genel Sağlık Sigortası (GSS) prim borçları ile bunlara bağlı gecikme cezası ve zamlarının tamamını siliyoruz. 2 milyon 199 bin 860 vatandaşımızın toplam 5 milyar 627 milyon 666 bin TL tutarındaki prim borcunu ortadan kaldırıyoruz.”

CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Güler, GSS prim borçları ile gecikme cezası ve zamlarının tamamen silinmesinin öngörüldüğünü açıkladı Düzenlemenin yasalaşması halinde 2 milyon 199 bin 860 kişinin toplam 5 milyar 627 milyon 666 bin liralık borcu ortadan kalkacak. Düzenlemeye ilişkin açıklamasında Güler, şu ifadeleri kullandı: “1 Ocak 2017 öncesine ait ödenmemiş Genel Sağlık Sigortası (GSS) prim borçları ile bunlara bağlı gecikme cezası ve zamlarının tamamını siliyoruz. 2 milyon 199 bin 860 vatandaşımızın toplam 5 milyar 627 milyon 666 bin TL tutarındaki prim borcunu ortadan kaldırıyoruz.”

news.title: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
news.summary: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
news.summaryTr: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.
news.articleText: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century - Published Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%, congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. The contest was not considered to be in play until the final weeks of the campaign, given President Donald Trump won the state in the 2024 election by more than 22 points. Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky. Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election. "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said. "It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did." "In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference." Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced. The room burst into deafening applause and cheers. "This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board. "This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising. "This is a historic election." Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory. "When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy." The last black senator in the state before Colom was Bruce who was chosen by the state legislature. It has taken a century and a half for the state to choose a new one, this time by Mississippi voters. In his campaign, Colom strove to engage Republican voters, even going to a Trump rally to speak to people in line outside. Another key moment was his opponent telling voters to "pick another protein" when asked about surging beef prices, something Colom turned into a viral advert of his own., external Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans. Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls. Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices". The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties. Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns. The 67-year-old Republican was criticised for a lack of public appearances. Democrats have scored a series of major wins in these midterm elections, taking control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate. The party flipped Senate seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. news.title: Dünyayı kurtaran haber | Hidrojen ekonomisi için 7 milyar dolarlık yatırım yapıldı
news.summary: Yeşil hidrojen, enerji dönüşümünde sanayi ve ağır taşımacılık sektörlerinin yeni enerji kaynaklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor. IEA göre, düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik küresel yatırım geçen yıl yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Dünyayı kurtaran haber | Hidrojen ekonomisi için 7 milyar dolarlık yatırım yapıldı
news.summaryTr: Yeşil hidrojen, enerji dönüşümünde sanayi ve ağır taşımacılık sektörlerinin yeni enerji kaynaklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor. IEA göre, düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik küresel yatırım geçen yıl yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı.
news.articleText: Dünyayı kurtaran haber | Hidrojen ekonomisi için 7 milyar dolarlık yatırım yapıldı - Yeşil hidrojen, enerji dönüşümünde sanayi ve ağır taşımacılık sektörlerinin yeni enerji kaynaklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor. - Elektrolizör üretiminden hidrojen boru hatlarına, depolama tesislerinden amonyak ve çelik üretimine uzanan yeni bir değer zinciri oluşuyor. - Uluslararası Enerji Ajansı'na (IEA) göre, düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik küresel yatırım geçen yıl yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı. İlandır Uluslararası Enerji Ajansı'nın (IEA) Eylül 2026'da yayımladığı Global Hydrogen Review 2026 raporuna göre, elektroliz yoluyla hidrojen üretiminde kurulu küresel kapasite 2025'te iki katına çıkarak 4 GW'ı aştı. Bu artışta Çin'de devreye alınan büyük ölçekli projeler etkili oldu. Ayrıca 2,5 GW'ın üzerinde elektrolizör kapasitesinin inşaatı devam ediyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik sermaye harcamaları da 2025'te yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, 2024'teki seviyenin yaklaşık iki katına çıktı. IEA, elektrolizör yatırımlarının 2026'da düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik toplam yatırımın yaklaşık yüzde 70'ini oluşturmasını bekliyor. Çin, elektrolizör kapasitesi ve üretiminde öne çıkan ülkeler arasında yer alırken Avrupa da büyük ölçekli projeler geliştiriyor. Bununla birlikte, küresel hidrojen üretiminde fosil yakıtlara dayalı yöntemler ağırlığını koruyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen üretimi 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 1 milyon tona ulaştı. Bu miktar, toplam hidrojen üretiminin hâlâ küçük bir bölümünü oluşturdu. Sanayi ve gübre üretimi yeni talep alanları oluşturuyor Hidrojenin mevcut kullanım alanlarının başında petrol rafinerileri, amonyak üretimi ve kimya sanayisi geliyor. Bugün kullanılan hidrojenin büyük bölümü bu geleneksel sektörlerde tüketiliyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin yaygınlaşmasıyla birlikte mevcut üretim süreçlerinin daha düşük karbonlu yöntemlere dönüştürülmesi hedefleniyor. Gübre sanayisinde amonyak üretimi, hidrojen talebinin önemli kaynaklarından birini oluşturuyor. Hidrojen, amonyak üretiminin temel girdilerinden biri olduğu için yenilenebilir kaynaklardan üretilmesi, gübre sektörünün emisyonlarının azaltılmasında rol oynayabiliyor. Kimya sanayisinde ise metanol gibi hidrojen temelli ürünlerin üretimi yeni kullanım alanları arasında bulunuyor. Çelik üretimi de hidrojen ekonomisinin gelişebileceği sektörlerden biri. Demir cevherinin doğrudan indirgenmesi sürecinde kullanılan hidrojen, kömür ve doğal gaz temelli yöntemlere alternatif oluşturabiliyor. Bu alandaki yatırımlar, hidrojen üreticilerinin yanı sıra çelik tesisleri, ekipman üreticileri ve enerji altyapısı şirketleri için de yeni pazarlar yaratıyor. IEA'nın değerlendirmesine göre, yatırım kararı alınmış düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projeleri kapsamında 2030'a kadar rafineriler ve sanayi tesislerinde 2,5 milyon ton hidrojenin üretilip tüketilmesi bekleniyor. Hidrojenin taşınması ve depolanması için altyapı kuruluyor Hidrojenin sanayide ve taşımacılıkta daha geniş ölçekte kullanılabilmesi, yalnızca üretim kapasitesinin artırılmasına bağlı değil. Üretilen hidrojenin tüketim merkezlerine ulaştırılması, depolanması ve farklı sektörlere dağıtılması için yeni altyapı yatırımları gerekiyor. IEA'nın Global Hydrogen Review 2026 raporuna göre, 2035'e kadar devreye alınması planlanan hidrojen boru hatlarının toplam uzunluğu 40 bin kilometreyi aşıyor. Ancak açıklanan projelerin yalnızca yüzde 9'u işletmede veya yatırım kararı alınmış durumda. Bazı projelerde mevcut doğal gaz boru hatlarının hidrojen taşımacılığına uygun hale getirilmesi de planlanıyor. Yer altı hidrojen depolama projeleri de altyapı yatırımlarının bir diğer ayağını oluşturuyor. Açıklanan projelerin tamamlanması halinde 2035'e kadar yaklaşık 11 teravatsaatlik depolama kapasitesine ulaşılması öngörülüyor. Ancak bu kapasitenin yüzde 7'sinden biraz fazlası yatırım kararı almış veya inşaat aşamasına geçmiş durumda. Hidrojenin uluslararası ticaretinde ise boru hatlarının yanı sıra amonyak ve metanol gibi hidrojen türevlerinin taşınması öne çıkıyor. Bu ürünler, hidrojenin gemilerle taşınmasını ve mevcut liman altyapısının belirli ölçüde kullanılmasını mümkün kılıyor. Ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojenli araç pazarı Hidrojenin yeni kullanım alanlarından biri de ağır taşımacılık. Yakıt hücreli araçlarda hidrojen, elektrik üretmek için kullanılıyor ve elektrik motoru aracın hareketini sağlıyor. Bu teknoloji özellikle uzun mesafeli kamyon taşımacılığı ve otobüsler için geliştirilen seçenekler arasında yer alıyor. IEA'ya göre, yakıt hücreli elektrikli araçların küresel sayısı 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 130 bine ulaştı. Artışta Çin'deki kamyon satışları ve Güney Kore'deki binek araç pazarı etkili oldu. Ajansın değerlendirmesinde, 2030'a kadar yakıt hücreli araç sayısının üç katına çıkabileceği, bu araçlar arasındaki hidrojen kullanımında kamyonların yaklaşık yüzde 60, otobüslerin ise yüzde 30 pay alabileceği öngörülüyor. Bununla birlikte hidrojenli araçların yaygınlaşması, üretim tesislerinin yanı sıra yakıt ikmal istasyonları, depolama sistemleri ve dağıtım ağlarının kurulmasını gerektiriyor. Bu nedenle ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojen pazarı, araç üretiminin yanında yeni bir enerji tedarik zincirinin gelişmesine de bağlı. Hidrojen ekonomisinin büyümesinde maliyetler ve talep belirleyici olmaya devam ediyor. IEA, düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin kısa vadede dünyanın büyük bölümünde fosil yakıtlardan üretilen hidrojene kıyasla daha pahalı kalacağını belirtiyor. Projelerin hayata geçirilmesi için üretim desteğinin yanı sıra sanayi kuruluşlarının uzun vadeli alım taahhütleri ve taşıma-depolama altyapısının geliştirilmesi gerekiyor.

CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik sermaye harcamaları da 2025'te yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, 2024'teki seviyenin yaklaşık iki katına çıktı. IEA, elektrolizör yatırımlarının 2026'da düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik toplam yatırımın yaklaşık yüzde 70'ini oluşturmasını bekliyor. Çin, elektrolizör kapasitesi ve üretiminde öne çıkan ülkeler arasında yer alırken Avrupa da büyük ölçekli projeler geliştiriyor. Bununla birlikte, küresel hidrojen üretiminde fosil yakıtlara dayalı yöntemler ağırlığını koruyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen üretimi 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 1 milyon tona ulaştı. Bu miktar, toplam hidrojen üretiminin hâlâ küçük bir bölümünü oluşturdu. Sanayi ve gübre üretimi yeni talep alanları oluşturuyor Hidrojenin mevcut kullanım alanlarının başında petrol rafinerileri, amonyak üretimi ve kimya sanayisi geliyor. Bugün kullanılan hidrojenin büyük bölümü bu geleneksel sektörlerde tüketiliyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin yaygınlaşmasıyla birlikte mevcut üretim süreçlerinin daha düşük karbonlu yöntemlere dönüştürülmesi hedefleniyor. Gübre sanayisinde amonyak üretimi, hidrojen talebinin önemli kaynaklarından birini oluşturuyor. Hidrojen, amonyak üretiminin temel girdilerinden biri olduğu için yenilenebilir kaynaklardan üretilmesi, gübre sektörünün emisyonlarının azaltılmasında rol oynayabiliyor. Kimya sanayisinde ise metanol gibi hidrojen temelli ürünlerin üretimi yeni kullanım alanları arasında bulunuyor. Çelik üretimi de hidrojen ekonomisinin gelişebileceği sektörlerden biri. Demir cevherinin doğrudan indirgenmesi sürecinde kullanılan hidrojen, kömür ve doğal gaz temelli yöntemlere alternatif oluşturabiliyor. Bu alandaki yatırımlar, hidrojen üreticilerinin yanı sıra çelik tesisleri, ekipman üreticileri ve enerji altyapısı şirketleri için de yeni pazarlar yaratıyor. IEA'nın değerlendirmesine göre, yatırım kararı alınmış düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projeleri kapsamında 2030'a kadar rafineriler ve sanayi tesislerinde 2,5 milyon ton hidrojenin üretilip tüketilmesi bekleniyor. Hidrojenin taşınması ve depolanması için altyapı kuruluyor Hidrojenin sanayide ve taşımacılıkta daha geniş ölçekte kullanılabilmesi, yalnızca üretim kapasitesinin artırılmasına bağlı değil. Üretilen hidrojenin tüketim merkezlerine ulaştırılması, depolanması ve farklı sektörlere dağıtılması için yeni altyapı yatırımları gerekiyor. IEA'nın Global Hydrogen Review 2026 raporuna göre, 2035'e kadar devreye alınması planlanan hidrojen boru hatlarının toplam uzunluğu 40 bin kilometreyi aşıyor. Ancak açıklanan projelerin yalnızca yüzde 9'u işletmede veya yatırım kararı alınmış durumda. Bazı projelerde mevcut doğal gaz boru hatlarının hidrojen taşımacılığına uygun hale getirilmesi de planlanıyor. Yer altı hidrojen depolama projeleri de altyapı yatırımlarının bir diğer ayağını oluşturuyor. Açıklanan projelerin tamamlanması halinde 2035'e kadar yaklaşık 11 teravatsaatlik depolama kapasitesine ulaşılması öngörülüyor. Ancak bu kapasitenin yüzde 7'sinden biraz fazlası yatırım kararı almış veya inşaat aşamasına geçmiş durumda. Hidrojenin uluslararası ticaretinde ise boru hatlarının yanı sıra amonyak ve metanol gibi hidrojen türevlerinin taşınması öne çıkıyor. Bu ürünler, hidrojenin gemilerle taşınmasını ve mevcut liman altyapısının belirli ölçüde kullanılmasını mümkün kılıyor. Ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojenli araç pazarı Hidrojenin yeni kullanım alanlarından biri de ağır taşımacılık. Yakıt hücreli araçlarda hidrojen, elektrik üretmek için kullanılıyor ve elektrik motoru aracın hareketini sağlıyor. Bu teknoloji özellikle uzun mesafeli kamyon taşımacılığı ve otobüsler için geliştirilen seçenekler arasında yer alıyor. IEA'ya göre, yakıt hücreli elektrikli araçların küresel sayısı 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 130 bine ulaştı. Artışta Çin'deki kamyon satışları ve Güney Kore'deki binek araç pazarı etkili oldu. Ajansın değerlendirmesinde, 2030'a kadar yakıt hücreli araç sayısının üç katına çıkabileceği, bu araçlar arasındaki hidrojen kullanımında kamyonların yaklaşık yüzde 60, otobüslerin ise yüzde 30 pay alabileceği öngörülüyor. Bununla birlikte hidrojenli araçların yaygınlaşması, üretim tesislerinin yanı sıra yakıt ikmal istasyonları, depolama sistemleri ve dağıtım ağlarının kurulmasını gerektiriyor. Bu nedenle ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojen pazarı, araç üretiminin yanında yeni bir enerji tedarik zincirinin gelişmesine de bağlı. Hidrojen ekonomisinin büyümesinde maliyetler ve talep belirleyici olmaya devam ediyor. IEA, düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin kısa vadede dünyanın büyük bölümünde fosil yakıtlardan üretilen hidrojene kıyasla daha pahalı kalacağını belirtiyor. Projelerin hayata geçirilmesi için üretim desteğinin yanı sıra sanayi kuruluşlarının uzun vadeli alım taahhütleri ve taşıma-depolama altyapısının geliştirilmesi gerekiyor.

news.summary: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
news.summaryTr: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
news.articleText: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says - Published Six people have been killed and about 20 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says. The hospital's director said two missiles hit a building containing surgical wards and intensive care units overnight, but that one of the missiles did not explode. The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions". The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces. Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime". Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war. Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies. Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory. The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people. In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department. Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion. The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded. "What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said. "Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital." Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts. News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile. Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion. "My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC. "I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all." He said he had been lying in a bed near Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, who was killed. Another colleague suffered a broken leg. "Dr Rizq was the kindest person in this department. He was very kind and always willing to help... And of course, he was a surgeon, one of the best among us." He added: "Patients were killed as well. There were patients in the rooms next to us who were killed. A patient comes to the hospital seeking treatment and leaves carried on people's shoulders. I do not know what kind of humanity this is." The Israeli military said in a statement that its "precise strike" had targeted the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, who it named as Mohammed Abu Ismail, alongside other fighters who were "hiding inside" Nasser hospital. "The terrorists were struck in order to remove the threat they posed after turning the Nasser hospital compound into a headquarters and operating from there to advance dozens of terrorist plots against our forces and restore the brigade's force," it alleged. The military added that it had issued advance warnings before the strike and released an audio recording of what it said was one given to a senior Gaza health official. But Fara insisted the hospital had received no warning of an attack. A Hamas statement rejected the Israeli military's accusations, calling them "a blatant attempt to justify a documented crime targeting a civilian medical facility whose function and purpose are well known". "The nature of the targeted site and the casualties inflicted on patients, doctors and medical staff expose the falsity and weakness of this narrative," it said. However, local activists circulated claims overnight that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building. Fara said this was the seventh time that Nasser hospital had been struck during the war. In August 2025, a double Israeli strike killed 22 Palestinians, including journalists and health workers. Israeli strikes on Gaza take place almost daily despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas in October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the same period. The humanitarian situation in Gaza also remains dire and has recently deteriorated further as a result of heavy rains last weekend that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

items.articleText: AJet'ten Almanya hamlesi: Anadolu'dan 6 kente 26 yeni direkt hat - AJet, 2027 yaz sezonunda Trabzon, Samsun, Sivas, Çukurova ve Gaziantep'ten Almanya'nın 6 kentine açacağı 26 yeni direkt hattın biletlerini satışa sundu. Yeni bağlantılar kapsamında haftada toplam 34 karşılıklı sefer düzenlenecek. AJet, 2027 yaz sezonunda Trabzon, Samsun, Sivas, Çukurova ve Gaziantep ile Almanya arasında açacağı yeni direkt hatların biletlerini satışa sundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketten yapılan açıklamaya göre, Anadolu’dan Almanya’nın 6 kentine haftada toplam 34 karşılıklı sefer düzenlenecek. Yeni hatlarla Almanya’da yaşayan Türk vatandaşlarının memleketlerine ulaşımının kolaylaştırılması ve bölge turizmine katkı sağlanması hedefleniyor. AJet, Çukurova Uluslararası Havalimanı’ndan Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Münih ve Stuttgart’a haftada toplam 7 karşılıklı sefer gerçekleştirecek. Samsun Çarşamba ve Trabzon havalimanlarından Berlin, Köln, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Münih ve Stuttgart’a haftada toplam 24 sefer planlanırken, Sivas-Köln hattında haftada 2, Gaziantep-Düsseldorf hattında ise haftada 1 karşılıklı sefer yapılacak. Çukurova çıkışlı uçuşlar ile Samsun’dan Düsseldorf ve Münih’e, Trabzon’dan Frankfurt ve Stuttgart’a seferler Nisan 2027’de başlayacak. Diğer hatlarda ise uçuşların Haziran 2027’de başlaması planlanıyor. "Anadolu ile Almanya arasında yeni bir hava köprüsü kuruyoruz" AJet Genel Müdürü Kerem Sarp, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, "Anadolu ile Almanya arasında yeni bir hava köprüsü kuruyoruz." ifadesini kullandı. Sarp, "Kısa süre önce Bodrum ve Dalaman hatlarımızı duyurmuştuk. Bugün de Almanya ile Trabzon, Samsun, Sivas, Çukurova ve Gaziantep arasındaki 26 yeni direkt hattımızın biletlerini satışa sunuyoruz." bilgisini verdi. Yeni bağlantıların yurt dışında yaşayan vatandaşların seyahatlerini kolaylaştıracağını vurgulayan Sarp, şunları kaydetti: "Bu seferlerle Almanya’da yaşayan vatandaşlarımızın memleketlerine ve sevdiklerine aktarmasız ulaşmasını kolaylaştırıyoruz. Yeni bağlantılarımızın Anadolu’yu keşfetmek isteyen misafirlerimize daha fazla seçenek sunacağına ve bölge turizmine katkı sağlayacağına inanıyorum. Türkiye’nin en genç ve en hızlı büyüyen hava yolu olarak misafirlerimize daha fazla noktaya erişilebilir ve güvenli seyahat imkanı sunmak için çalışmaya devam edeceğiz. Yeni hatlarımızın şimdiden hayırlı olmasını diliyorum." AJet, daha önce de 2027 yaz döneminde Bodrum ve Dalaman’dan Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Hannover ve Münih’e düzenlenecek direkt seferlerin biletlerini satışa sunmuştu.

Yeni hatlarımızın şimdiden hayırlı olmasını diliyorum." AJet, daha önce de 2027 yaz döneminde Bodrum ve Dalaman’dan Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Hannover ve Münih’e düzenlenecek direkt seferlerin biletlerini satışa sunmuştu.

items.titleTr: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente
items.summaryTr: Crypto hackers stole $8.7 billion so far in 2026, surpassing the projected annual onchain revenue generated across the industry, according to ARK’s research director.
items.articleText: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente Crypto hackers stole $8.7 billion so far in 2026, surpassing the projected annual onchain revenue generated across the industry, according to ARK’s research director. Hackers stole 57 cents for every $1 earned onchain by blockchain protocols since 2017, according to Lorenzo Valente, director of digital asset research at ARK Investment Management. “Security is the bottleneck,” wrote Valente in a Thursday X post, sharing a chart showing that $8.7 billion lost to crypto hacks year to date had already surpassed the $5.6 billion in estimated annual onchain revenue for 2026. Since 2017, the crypto industry has lost about $26.9 billion to hacks and earned $47 billion in total onchain revenue, he added. The recent $6.3 billion stolen in the Binance hack alone exceeded Valente’s estimate for full-year 2026 onchain revenue. Value lost to hacks is on track to exceed onchain revenue by year-end for the first time since 2020. The crypto industry saw a string of high-value hacks this year, including September’s $387 million Bitget hack and the $320 million Liquid Network exploit, as well as April’s $295 million Drift Protocol exploit. The mounting security exploits are weighing on the institutional appetite for DeFi. In an April research note, JPMorgan analysts identified bridge security as a long-standing challenge for the industry. Total value locked in decentralized finance (DeFi) has fallen nearly 10% since the Binance exploit, from $85.9 billion on Oct. 29 to $77.4 billion on Thursday, according to DefiLlama. Related: Binance warns iOS flaw could expose crypto wallet keys

items.titleTr: Are Alt-L1s over? Security, costs drive smaller chains to Ethereum
items.summaryTr: L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist.
items.articleText: Are Alt-L1s over? Security, costs drive smaller chains to Ethereum L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist. Running an independent blockchain has always come with a particular promise: control. A standalone Layer 1 architecture allows projects to be the masters of their own destiny, set the rules of consensus, maintain their own validators and build infrastructure around their users, without relying on any other network. But with great power comes great responsibility — and considerable expense. Blockchains need enough users, developers and economic activity to support the infrastructure that secures them. For some smaller networks, keeping an entire ecosystem afloat no longer makes economic sense. Zilliqa is the latest project to confront that reality, announcing plans last week to move away from its L1 architecture and become an Ethereum-based Layer 2 (L2) instead: “We know it’s not great. For nine years we built and ran our own Layer 1. It hasn’t worked.” “Usage never reached what a standalone chain needs,” the post explained. “Funding and liquidity for standalone L1s dried up. The recent hacks showed how much it takes to secure a chain alone. The data is onchain for everyone to see.” Zilliqa is not alone. Blockchain ecosystem Gnosis (which has always been Ethereum-adjacent) is also working to transition Gnosis Chain into an Ethereum-based network through its Ethereum Economic Zone (EEZ) initiative. Its RollupX test network intends to show how participating chains can share Ethereum settlement and synchronous composability as native rollups. Gaming-focused Ronin blockchain also completed its move back to Ethereum as an L2 in May. With interest in alt L1s drying up along with the funding, will we start to see more and more chains consolidating in the Ethereum ecosystem? The cost of going it alone Independent L1s generally have to keep several core functions going, including execution, consensus, data availability and settlement. They must also fund the token incentives used to secure their networks through staking. Related: What are native rollups? Full guide to Ethereum’s latest innovation “It comes down to a chain’s profitability,” Max Shannon, senior research analyst at Bitwise, tells Magazine. ZIL becomes a Layer 2 on Ethereum. Source: Zilliqa “L2s only need to maintain execution and do not necessarily need a token, which makes them a more attractive financial and operational proposition,” he says. Shannon says the top ten largest projects are more financially sustainable. Coinbase and Robinhood’s L2 networks generated $48 million and $52 million in fees respectively over the last 365 days, with margins above 90%. The next eight largest chains each generated more than $1 million annually. From 11th place onward, however, annual fees collectively amounted to less than $1 million. So a network may have ambitious technology and a dedicated community, but those things don’t necessarily pay the bills. Ethereum is often criticized for giving away too much of its revenue to L2s, but that’s precisely what makes it attractive to set up projects there. But just becoming an Ethereum L2 doesn’t automatically make a network profitable however. Shannon points to Optimism, Katana and Linea as examples of networks whose expenses outweigh their fee revenue. Projects like Blast have already been forced to shut down. Ethereum as a liquidity ‘black hole’ Gnosis has targeted spring 2027 to complete its transition, which will see it give up its independent validator-based consensus in favor of Ethereum settlement. Gnosis Chain will relaunch as an Ethereum Economic Zone. Source: Gnosis “Two years ago I gave a talk about ‘native Rollups’ that would truly extend Ethereum instead of being isolated chains,” co-founder Martin Köppelmann said, adding that RollupX “even goes beyond what I had imagined back then!” Gnosis’s EEZ initiative aims to enable separate Ethereum-based networks interact synchronously, so a smart contract on one network can call another and use its response within the same transaction, without relying on the usual bridge-and-wait process. That’s a prospect that has some Ethereum supporters particularly bullish, with ETH bull materkel describing the EEZ as a potential “black hole for liquidity,” and saying it could allow participating networks to tap into Ethereum’s total value locked (TVL) and strengthen its position as a liquidity hub. Could network effects, and increased interoperability draw more and more chains into Ethereum’s orbit? Beyond the cost savings It isn’t only the operating cost economics that make sense. Projects can also tap into an established ecosystem of applications and developers rather than building those network effects from scratch. Related: Privacy tools are rising behind institutional adoption, says ZKsync dev Alex Gluchowski, co-founder and chief executive of Matter Labs, the company behind Ethereum L2 ZKsync, says he expects more L1 teams to maintain their own chains while using Ethereum for settlement. “Running an independent L1 means maintaining its security as well as building something people want to use,” Gluchowski tells Magazine. “Sharing Ethereum’s security gives a team more room to focus on its users. I see very few user needs that require an independent L1 rather than an Ethereum-based chain.” But Gluchowski says sovereignty and Ethereum integration are not mutually exclusive, since chains can retain control over their rules and operations while using Ethereum for shared settlement. Ronin completed migration to Ethereum in May. Source: Ronin And for applications handling sensitive financial information, maintaining a private environment under their own control can be essential, he says. Shared settlement does not have to mean exposing confidential transaction data. The biggest obstacle today is that all the L2s are effectively isolated from each other and from Ethereum. It’s certainly possible to jump between them, but its far from seamless and interoperability is poor. “Fragmentation is already happening,” Gluchowski says, pointing to the difficulty of connecting networks when transactions involve privacy. Interoperability between private environments will become more important as more applications seek to combine confidential activity with access to public blockchain liquidity, he says. Does every chain need Ethereum? Shannon cautions against describing the market as undergoing straightforward consolidation around Ethereum. Some large institutions are launching L2 networks, he says, including Coinbase and Robinhood, but others are still choosing to build independent L1s, like Circle’s Arc, Stripe’s Tempo, or Hyperliquid’s purpose-specific perpetual futures blockchain. “So there is no clear conclusion to the L1 versus L2 debate as yet,” he says. items.articleText: Trump bu kez komşusunu hedef aldı: İki kat vergi tehdidi - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Meksika'ya göçmen kafileleri üzerinden yeni bir tarife tehdidinde bulundu. Trump, ABD sınırına ilerleyen göçmen gruplarının durdurulmaması halinde ülkeye uygulanan gümrük vergilerini derhal iki katına çıkaracağını açıkladı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Meksika'ya göçmen kafileleri üzerinden yeni bir gümrük vergisi tehdidinde bulundu. Trump, ABD sınırına doğru ilerleyen göçmen gruplarının durdurulmaması halinde Meksika'ya uygulanan gümrük tarifelerini derhal iki katına çıkaracağını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Cumhuriyetçilerin ara seçimlerde yaşadığı kayıpların ardından büyük göçmen kafilelerinin oluşmaya başladığını ileri süren Trump, ABD'ye yasa dışı yollarla giriş yapmak isteyenlerin ülkeye kabul edilmeyeceğini söyledi. Meksika'ya tarife uyarısı Meksika yönetimine göçmen kafilelerinin ilerleyişini engelleme çağrısı yapan Trump, aksi takdirde ülkeye yönelik gümrük vergilerinin artırılacağını belirtti. Trump, konuya ilişkin Meksikalı yetkililerin yanı sıra Teksas yönetimi, ABD Sınır Devriyesi ve Göçmenlik ve Gümrük Muhafaza Dairesinin (ICE) de bilgilendirildiğini kaydetti. ABD'nin sınır güvenliği konusundaki tutumunun değişmeyeceğini vurgulayan Trump, bu konuda herhangi bir taviz verilmeyeceğini ifade etti.

items.title: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
items.summary: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
items.summaryTr: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
items.articleText: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient - Published The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September. "Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy. It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War". Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth. It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity. The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic. The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%. Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago. This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France. It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise. Not a boom While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either. Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helpingboost growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes. While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week. Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment. I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss. However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year. Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again. There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed. The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf. Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too. Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy". - Published6 days ago - Published2 hours ago

items.articleText: Akbank'tan 2,5 trilyon TL'lik dev hedef: Kaan Gür COP31'de açıkladı - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, COP31 kapsamında CNBC-e'ye yaptığı açıklamada, bankanın 2030 yılına kadar 2,5 trilyon TL sürdürülebilir finansman sağlamayı hedeflediğini söyledi. Gür, bu tutarın yarısını sanayide yeşil dönüşüme ayırmayı planladıklarını belirtti. Antalya'da düzenlenen Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı'nda (COP31) CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtlayan Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman hedeflerini, sanayide yeşil dönüşüme yönelik çalışmalarını ve yeni iş birliklerini anlattı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Gür, Akbank'ın 9 Kasım'dan bu yana COP31'de 38 kişilik bir ekiple yer aldığını, zirve boyunca yaklaşık 35 etkinlik ve çeşitli imza törenleri gerçekleştireceklerini söyledi. COP31'de taahhütlerden uygulamaya geçiş konusunda güçlü bir kararlılık gördüklerini belirten Gür, Türkiye'nin coğrafi konumu, sanayi altyapısı ve entegrasyon kapasitesiyle dönüşümde liderlik fırsatına sahip olduğunu ifade etti. Gür, Türkiye'nin sanayide düşük karbonlu üretime geçişini hızlandırması halinde mevcut ihracat pazarlarındaki rekabet gücünü koruyabileceğini ve küresel tedarik zincirinde kendisini yeniden konumlandırabileceğini söyledi. Sürdürülebilir finansman desteği 905 milyar TL'yi aştı Akbank'ın sürdürülebilir finansman hedeflerine ilişkin bilgi veren Gür, 2021 yılında 200 milyar TL'lik finansman hedefiyle yola çıktıklarını, 2024 yılında ise bu hedefi 800 milyar TL'ye yükselttiklerini hatırlattı. Gür, bankanın bugüne kadar sağladığı toplam sürdürülebilir finansman desteğinin 905 milyar TL'yi aştığını belirterek, 2030 yılına kadar 2,5 trilyon TL'lik yeni bir hedef belirlediklerini açıkladı. Finansman büyüklüğünün yanı sıra ekonomiye sağlanan katkının da önemli olduğunu vurgulayan Gür, sağlanan finansmanın karbon emisyonlarını ne ölçüde azalttığı, rekabet gücüne ve istihdama ne kadar katkı sunduğu gibi göstergeleri takip ettiklerini ifade etti. Finansmanın yarısı sanayide yeşil dönüşüme Gür, 2,5 trilyon TL'lik sürdürülebilir finansman hedefinin yüzde 50'sini sanayide yeşil dönüşüme ayırmayı planladıklarını söyledi. Bu kapsamda sanayide yeşil dönüşüm için 1,25 trilyon TL'lik finansman öngörülüyor. Akbank'ın sürdürülebilir finansmanda öncelik verdiği alanları sanayide yeşil dönüşüm, sürdürülebilir tedarik zinciri, elektrifikasyon, sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme ve mavi finansman olarak sıralayan Gür, tarım bankacılığı, kadınların ekonomideki gücünün artırılması, gençlerin geleceğe hazırlanması ile sosyal ve dijital kapsayıcılığın da bankanın odak alanları arasında yer aldığını belirtti. Gür, sanayide yeşil dönüşümde finansman desteğinin yanı sıra teknoloji ve teknik yeterliliklerin de önem taşıdığını ifade ederek projelerin yapılabilir, kârlı ve geri ödenebilir bir yapıda kurgulanması gerektiğini söyledi. Uluslararası kuruluşlarla ortak finansman Türkiye'nin 2035 yılına kadar güneş ve rüzgâr enerjisinde 120 gigavatlık hedefi bulunduğunu hatırlatan Gür, enerji kapasitesinin artırılmasının yanı sıra şebeke altyapısı, enerji depolama ve elektrifikasyon alanlarında da yatırımlara ihtiyaç duyulduğunu belirtti. Akbank'ın Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (EBRD) ve Uluslararası Finans Kurumu (IFC) gibi uluslararası kuruluşlarla ortak fonlama imkânları geliştirdiğini aktaran Gür, teknoloji ve teknik beceriler konusunda da danışmanlık yaklaşımıyla hareket edeceklerini söyledi. Büyük işletmelerin üretim tesislerindeki dönüşümün yanı sıra tedarik zincirlerinde yer alan KOBİ'lerin de desteklenmesi gerektiğini belirten Gür, daha dirençli bir tarım ekosistemi, su verimliliği ve geri kazanım projelerinin de bankanın öncelikleri arasında bulunduğunu ifade etti. Gür, uluslararası finans kuruluşlarıyla yürütülen çalışmalar kapsamında yatırımcılara, sanayicilere ve KOBİ'lere farklı vade ve risk paylaşımı imkânları sunmayı hedeflediklerini kaydetti. Daikin ile yeni finansman program Gür, COP31 kapsamında Birleşmiş Milletler Kalkınma Programı'nın (UNDP) Cool Up programı çerçevesinde Daikin ile yeni bir sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme finansman programına imza attıklarını açıkladı. Programdan ağırlıklı olarak KOBİ'lerin yararlanacağını belirten Gür, soğuk zincir, depolama, lojistik ve sağlık sektörlerinde enerji verimliliğinin artırılması ve karbon emisyonlarının azaltılmasına yönelik yatırımların destekleneceğini söyledi. Türkiye'deki enerji tüketiminin yaklaşık yüzde 48'inin binalardan kaynaklandığını belirten Gür, binalardaki enerji tüketiminin üçte birini ise iklimlendirme sistemlerinin oluşturduğunu ifade etti. Gür, program kapsamında Daikin'in teknoloji, Akbank'ın finansman, Frankfurt School of Finance and Management'ın ise teknik destek sağladığını belirtti. Yeni iş birlikleri devam edecek Sürdürülebilir tedarik zinciri finansmanına da değinen Gür, Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası ile 2025 yılında başlattıkları risk paylaşımlı finansman programının gelişerek devam ettiğini söyledi. Gür, önümüzdeki dönemde yeni iş birliklerinin süreceğini belirterek Akbank'ın sanayicilere, KOBİ'lere ve müşterilerine yeşil dönüşüm sürecinde destek vermeye devam edeceğini ifade etti.

items.titleTr: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services
items.summaryTr: The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments.
items.articleText: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments. UK-based digital bank Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B round led by Octagon Partners, valuing the company at over $100 million. The funding will support Griffin’s plans to expand into card issuance and stablecoin services, according to a Thursday press release. Griffin plans to let companies offer branded retail and corporate debit cards through its platform, with credit cards to follow. The bank also plans to expand its stablecoin reserve services and add onchain cross-border payments. Griffin’s said its banking platform serves more than 300,000 retail and business customers through more than 80 companies. They include Uber, which uses Griffin to provide bank accounts to UK drivers. Griffin received its UK banking license in March 2024. The bank said recurring revenue at its September fiscal year-end was 3.2 times the prior year’s level, based on unaudited accounts. Paraag Davé, managing partner at Octagon, said he expects Griffin’s annual recurring revenue to exceed 10 million British pounds soon. Related: Deutsche Bank launches crypto custody for companies and institutions

items.summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.

items.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
items.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
items.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment. Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. Of the four million people claiming Pip in England and Wales, around 430,000 are aged between 16 and 24. In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. "I don't think you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them get into work," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme. 'Cannot assume' Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. 'Rebuilding system from scratch' In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. Disability groups have welcomed extra employment support, but expressed concern that disabled young people could lose out. James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" for young disabled people and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear". Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details families were "deeply anxious" about what they could mean for them. A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence. Responding on Thursday, Tory shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said Milburn was "right to say it's time to stop handing out cash for mild conditions". But she raised concern that spending more on work placements would simply "compensate for the jobs Labour have killed with their taxes and red tape". If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said. His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support. "It is a contract. People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added. A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. Of the four million people claiming Pip in England and Wales, around 430,000 are aged between 16 and 24. In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. "I don't think you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them get into work," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme. 'Cannot assume' Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. 'Rebuilding system from scratch' In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. Disability groups have welcomed extra employment support, but expressed concern that disabled young people could lose out. James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" for young disabled people and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear". Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details families were "deeply anxious" about what they could mean for them. A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence. Responding on Thursday, Tory shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said Milburn was "right to say it's time to stop handing out cash for mild conditions". But she raised concern that spending more on work placements would simply "compensate for the jobs Labour have killed with their taxes and red tape". If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said. His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support. "It is a contract. People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added. A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month. items.articleText: 'We've got to run': Inside ruined Ukraine power plant under constant drone threat As peace talks between Ukraine and Russia continue, Ukrainians are facing a rolling schedule of planned power cuts because of intensified Russian attacks on their energy grid. Ukraine has responded by striking Russian oil refineries. Officials are concerned that life will quickly become unsustainable for millions of Ukrainians if power supplies cannot be maintained for at least four hours per day. Some privately warn that's close already, as some families are living with outages of up to 20 hours in Kyiv. Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson visits one of the country's power stations on the front lines of the war. Devastated by a direct ballistic missile strike, repair work is hampered by hourly air raids.

items.summary: Medical staff are going unpaid, lack proper training and are struggling with shortages of essential supplies, MSF warns
