items.titleTr: Millions of Ebola dollars going missing as virus spreads, medical charity warns
items.summaryTr: Medical staff are going unpaid, lack proper training and are struggling with shortages of essential supplies, MSF warns
items.articleText: Millions of Ebola dollars going missing as virus spreads, medical charity warns - Published Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) says while the outbreak remains "out of control", there is a "considerable disconnect" between what is disbursed and what gets to "patients, frontline workers and communities". "Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many frontline responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets," the charity says in a report. More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May. This makes it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded. MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised. This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest," it said. MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for. At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure. - What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? - Published15 September In its report, external, MSF cited "cases of healthcare workers not being paid or trained, ambulances left to run without fuel, a lack of supplies or support for frontline employees". It also mentioned Ebola monitoring "surveillance teams that exist on paper but are nowhere to be seen on the ground". "Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim. One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation. "Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres. According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency. MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent. It said the response was "too slow" in North Kivu province while Haut-Uélé remained "dramatically overlooked". In both provinces, MSF observed that teams were "inadequately resourced to respond effectively" with health facilities lacking essential items such as water, chlorine or triage systems. "This has turned some facilities into new centres of transmission, rather than places of care that contribute to containing the disease," MSF said. The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control. There are very few good roads in the area, making it very hard to travel around. The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria. On Wednesday, the last person infected with Ebola in Kenya was discharged, marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation. The Bundibugyo species is relatively rare and has no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way. items.summary: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.

items.titleTr: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
items.summaryTr: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.
items.articleText: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century - Published Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%, congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. The contest was not considered to be in play until the final weeks of the campaign, given President Donald Trump won the state in the 2024 election by more than 22 points. Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky. Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election. "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said. "It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did." "In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference." Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced. The room burst into deafening applause and cheers. "This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board. "This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising. "This is a historic election." Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory. "When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy." The last black senator in the state before Colom was Bruce who was chosen by the state legislature. It has taken a century and a half for the state to choose a new one, this time by Mississippi voters. In his campaign, Colom strove to engage Republican voters, even going to a Trump rally to speak to people in line outside. Another key moment was his opponent telling voters to "pick another protein" when asked about surging beef prices, something Colom turned into a viral advert of his own., external Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans. Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls. Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices". The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties. Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns. items.articleTextTr: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century - Published Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%, congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. The contest was not considered to be in play until the final weeks of the campaign, given President Donald Trump won the state in the 2024 election by more than 22 points. Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky. Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election. "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said. "It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did." "In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference." Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced. The room burst into deafening applause and cheers. "This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board. "This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising. "This is a historic election." Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory. "When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy." The last black senator in the state before Colom was Bruce who was chosen by the state legislature. It has taken a century and a half for the state to choose a new one, this time by Mississippi voters. In his campaign, Colom strove to engage Republican voters, even going to a Trump rally to speak to people in line outside. Another key moment was his opponent telling voters to "pick another protein" when asked about surging beef prices, something Colom turned into a viral advert of his own., external Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans. Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls. Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices". The Democrat campaigned aggressively, visiting all of Mississippi's 82 counties. Hyde-Smith's campaign assailed Colom as a puppet of billionaire liberal donor George Soros, whose family has helped fund the Democrat's political campaigns. The 67-year-old Republican was criticised for a lack of public appearances. Teklifle asli görev alanı olmamasına rağmen kanunla verilen görevle 17 Eylül itibariyle olağanüstü tasfiyeyi yürüten personellere ve bankalara mali ve idari sorumsuzluk getiriyoruz. Güler, kanun teklifinde olağanüstü tasfiye sürecinde görev alan personel ve bankalara ilişkin bir düzenleme bulunduğunu da belirtti.

items.summaryTr: Yeşil hidrojen, enerji dönüşümünde sanayi ve ağır taşımacılık sektörlerinin yeni enerji kaynaklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor. IEA göre, düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik küresel yatırım geçen yıl yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı.
items.articleText: Dünyayı kurtaran haber | Hidrojen ekonomisi için 7 milyar dolarlık yatırım yapıldı - Yeşil hidrojen, enerji dönüşümünde sanayi ve ağır taşımacılık sektörlerinin yeni enerji kaynaklarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor. - Elektrolizör üretiminden hidrojen boru hatlarına, depolama tesislerinden amonyak ve çelik üretimine uzanan yeni bir değer zinciri oluşuyor. - Uluslararası Enerji Ajansı'na (IEA) göre, düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik küresel yatırım geçen yıl yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı. İlandır Uluslararası Enerji Ajansı'nın (IEA) Eylül 2026'da yayımladığı Global Hydrogen Review 2026 raporuna göre, elektroliz yoluyla hidrojen üretiminde kurulu küresel kapasite 2025'te iki katına çıkarak 4 GW'ı aştı. Bu artışta Çin'de devreye alınan büyük ölçekli projeler etkili oldu. Ayrıca 2,5 GW'ın üzerinde elektrolizör kapasitesinin inşaatı devam ediyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik sermaye harcamaları da 2025'te yaklaşık 7 milyar dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, 2024'teki seviyenin yaklaşık iki katına çıktı. IEA, elektrolizör yatırımlarının 2026'da düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projelerine yönelik toplam yatırımın yaklaşık yüzde 70'ini oluşturmasını bekliyor. Çin, elektrolizör kapasitesi ve üretiminde öne çıkan ülkeler arasında yer alırken Avrupa da büyük ölçekli projeler geliştiriyor. Bununla birlikte, küresel hidrojen üretiminde fosil yakıtlara dayalı yöntemler ağırlığını koruyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojen üretimi 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 1 milyon tona ulaştı. Bu miktar, toplam hidrojen üretiminin hâlâ küçük bir bölümünü oluşturdu. Sanayi ve gübre üretimi yeni talep alanları oluşturuyor Hidrojenin mevcut kullanım alanlarının başında petrol rafinerileri, amonyak üretimi ve kimya sanayisi geliyor. Bugün kullanılan hidrojenin büyük bölümü bu geleneksel sektörlerde tüketiliyor. Düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin yaygınlaşmasıyla birlikte mevcut üretim süreçlerinin daha düşük karbonlu yöntemlere dönüştürülmesi hedefleniyor. Gübre sanayisinde amonyak üretimi, hidrojen talebinin önemli kaynaklarından birini oluşturuyor. Hidrojen, amonyak üretiminin temel girdilerinden biri olduğu için yenilenebilir kaynaklardan üretilmesi, gübre sektörünün emisyonlarının azaltılmasında rol oynayabiliyor. Kimya sanayisinde ise metanol gibi hidrojen temelli ürünlerin üretimi yeni kullanım alanları arasında bulunuyor. Çelik üretimi de hidrojen ekonomisinin gelişebileceği sektörlerden biri. Demir cevherinin doğrudan indirgenmesi sürecinde kullanılan hidrojen, kömür ve doğal gaz temelli yöntemlere alternatif oluşturabiliyor. Bu alandaki yatırımlar, hidrojen üreticilerinin yanı sıra çelik tesisleri, ekipman üreticileri ve enerji altyapısı şirketleri için de yeni pazarlar yaratıyor. IEA'nın değerlendirmesine göre, yatırım kararı alınmış düşük emisyonlu hidrojen projeleri kapsamında 2030'a kadar rafineriler ve sanayi tesislerinde 2,5 milyon ton hidrojenin üretilip tüketilmesi bekleniyor. Hidrojenin taşınması ve depolanması için altyapı kuruluyor Hidrojenin sanayide ve taşımacılıkta daha geniş ölçekte kullanılabilmesi, yalnızca üretim kapasitesinin artırılmasına bağlı değil. Üretilen hidrojenin tüketim merkezlerine ulaştırılması, depolanması ve farklı sektörlere dağıtılması için yeni altyapı yatırımları gerekiyor. IEA'nın Global Hydrogen Review 2026 raporuna göre, 2035'e kadar devreye alınması planlanan hidrojen boru hatlarının toplam uzunluğu 40 bin kilometreyi aşıyor. Ancak açıklanan projelerin yalnızca yüzde 9'u işletmede veya yatırım kararı alınmış durumda. Bazı projelerde mevcut doğal gaz boru hatlarının hidrojen taşımacılığına uygun hale getirilmesi de planlanıyor. Yer altı hidrojen depolama projeleri de altyapı yatırımlarının bir diğer ayağını oluşturuyor. Açıklanan projelerin tamamlanması halinde 2035'e kadar yaklaşık 11 teravatsaatlik depolama kapasitesine ulaşılması öngörülüyor. Ancak bu kapasitenin yüzde 7'sinden biraz fazlası yatırım kararı almış veya inşaat aşamasına geçmiş durumda. Hidrojenin uluslararası ticaretinde ise boru hatlarının yanı sıra amonyak ve metanol gibi hidrojen türevlerinin taşınması öne çıkıyor. Bu ürünler, hidrojenin gemilerle taşınmasını ve mevcut liman altyapısının belirli ölçüde kullanılmasını mümkün kılıyor. Ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojenli araç pazarı Hidrojenin yeni kullanım alanlarından biri de ağır taşımacılık. Yakıt hücreli araçlarda hidrojen, elektrik üretmek için kullanılıyor ve elektrik motoru aracın hareketini sağlıyor. Bu teknoloji özellikle uzun mesafeli kamyon taşımacılığı ve otobüsler için geliştirilen seçenekler arasında yer alıyor. IEA'ya göre, yakıt hücreli elektrikli araçların küresel sayısı 2025'te yüzde 20 artarak yaklaşık 130 bine ulaştı. Artışta Çin'deki kamyon satışları ve Güney Kore'deki binek araç pazarı etkili oldu. Ajansın değerlendirmesinde, 2030'a kadar yakıt hücreli araç sayısının üç katına çıkabileceği, bu araçlar arasındaki hidrojen kullanımında kamyonların yaklaşık yüzde 60, otobüslerin ise yüzde 30 pay alabileceği öngörülüyor. Bununla birlikte hidrojenli araçların yaygınlaşması, üretim tesislerinin yanı sıra yakıt ikmal istasyonları, depolama sistemleri ve dağıtım ağlarının kurulmasını gerektiriyor. Bu nedenle ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojen pazarı, araç üretiminin yanında yeni bir enerji tedarik zincirinin gelişmesine de bağlı. Hidrojen ekonomisinin büyümesinde maliyetler ve talep belirleyici olmaya devam ediyor. IEA, düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin kısa vadede dünyanın büyük bölümünde fosil yakıtlardan üretilen hidrojene kıyasla daha pahalı kalacağını belirtiyor. Projelerin hayata geçirilmesi için üretim desteğinin yanı sıra sanayi kuruluşlarının uzun vadeli alım taahhütleri ve taşıma-depolama altyapısının geliştirilmesi gerekiyor.

Bununla birlikte hidrojenli araçların yaygınlaşması, üretim tesislerinin yanı sıra yakıt ikmal istasyonları, depolama sistemleri ve dağıtım ağlarının kurulmasını gerektiriyor. Bu nedenle ağır taşımacılıkta hidrojen pazarı, araç üretiminin yanında yeni bir enerji tedarik zincirinin gelişmesine de bağlı. Hidrojen ekonomisinin büyümesinde maliyetler ve talep belirleyici olmaya devam ediyor. IEA, düşük emisyonlu hidrojenin kısa vadede dünyanın büyük bölümünde fosil yakıtlardan üretilen hidrojene kıyasla daha pahalı kalacağını belirtiyor. Projelerin hayata geçirilmesi için üretim desteğinin yanı sıra sanayi kuruluşlarının uzun vadeli alım taahhütleri ve taşıma-depolama altyapısının geliştirilmesi gerekiyor.

items.titleTr: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
items.summaryTr: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
items.articleText: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says - Published Six people have been killed and about 20 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says. The hospital's director said two missiles hit a building containing surgical wards and intensive care units overnight, but that one of the missiles did not explode. The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions". The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces. Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime". Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war. Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies. Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory. The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people. In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department. Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion. The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded. "What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said. "Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital." Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts. News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile. Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion. "My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC. "I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all." He said he had been lying in a bed near Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, who was killed. Another colleague suffered a broken leg. "Dr Rizq was the kindest person in this department. He was very kind and always willing to help... And of course, he was a surgeon, one of the best among us." He added: "Patients were killed as well. There were patients in the rooms next to us who were killed. A patient comes to the hospital seeking treatment and leaves carried on people's shoulders. I do not know what kind of humanity this is." The Israeli military said in a statement that its "precise strike" had targeted the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, who it named as Mohammed Abu Ismail, alongside other fighters who were "hiding inside" Nasser hospital. "The terrorists were struck in order to remove the threat they posed after turning the Nasser hospital compound into a headquarters and operating from there to advance dozens of terrorist plots against our forces and restore the brigade's force," it alleged. The military added that it had issued advance warnings before the strike and released an audio recording of what it said was one given to a senior Gaza health official. But Fara insisted the hospital had received no warning of an attack. A Hamas statement rejected the Israeli military's accusations, calling them "a blatant attempt to justify a documented crime targeting a civilian medical facility whose function and purpose are well known". "The nature of the targeted site and the casualties inflicted on patients, doctors and medical staff expose the falsity and weakness of this narrative," it said. However, local activists circulated claims overnight that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building. Fara said this was the seventh time that Nasser hospital had been struck during the war. In August 2025, a double Israeli strike killed 22 Palestinians, including journalists and health workers. Israeli strikes on Gaza take place almost daily despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas in October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the same period. The humanitarian situation in Gaza also remains dire and has recently deteriorated further as a result of heavy rains last weekend that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

Merkez Bankası'nın 2026 yıl sonu enflasyon tahmini yüzde 29,5, 2027 yıl sonu tahmini yüzde 21, 2028 yüzde 13,5 oldu.

items.title: Süt üretiminde eylül tablosu: Toplanan inek sütü 962 bin tona yaklaştı
items.summary: TÜİK verilerine göre, ticari süt işletmelerince toplanan inek sütü miktarı eylülde yıllık yüzde 7,7 artarak 961 bin 915 tona çıktı. Ancak miktar ağustosa göre yüzde 5,8 geriledi. Ocak-eylül döneminde ise süt toplama miktarı yüzde 3,3 yükseldi.
